name: prismantis
description: Colorful, themeable rendering for Claude Code replies: tables, headings, code, numbers, paths and links.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Draw replies with this mod. Off falls back to Claude Code's own renderer.

theme.title: Theme
theme.description: Base palette, from popular MIT-licensed themes. Light variants: catppuccin-latte, gruvbox-light, rose-pine-dawn, github-light, solarized-light. mono uses bold and dim only. random picks a dark color preset each time the mod loads (session start or reload).

headingStyle.title: Heading style
headingStyle.description: Terminals have one font size, so headings get weight instead: banner (a box around H1, a heavy rule under H2), bold, underline, or uppercase H1.

tableStyle.title: Table style
tableStyle.description: box: every cell boxed, with a double line under the header. rules: a rule under the header and between rows. grid: heavier header rule, wider gaps. minimal: header rule only.

promptStyle.title: Your prompt style
promptStyle.description: How the prompts you type draw in the transcript. bubble: a rounded box in the accent color. wide: the same box across the full width, a divider between turns. bar: an accent bar on the left. chevron: a bold accent › before the text. off: Claude Code's own look.

clock.title: Clock times
clock.description: Shows when you sent each prompt and when each turn finished. 24h: 14:32. 12h: 2:32 PM. A time from another day gets its date. off: no times.

toolStyle.title: Tool row style
toolStyle.description: How tool rows (Ran, Read, Edited) sit next to Claude's sentences. chat: tool rows dimmed on the right, Claude on the left. tree-dim: tucked under the sentence with ⎿ and dimmed. tree-bold: tree-dim plus one-line sentences in bold. classic: the original look.

toolOutput.title: Tool output
toolOutput.description: How much of a tool call shows. full: what Claude Code shows. quiet: rows say in plain words what a call did, reads, searches and listings show only their row, other shell commands show their first lines, edits keep their diff, a failed call shows the last line of its error, and a refused call its full reason. Needs toolRows on.

taskStyle.title: Task list style
taskStyle.description: How - [ ] and - [x] items draw. checks: [ ] and [✓] with done items dimmed and struck through. ticks: ○ and ✓, done items dimmed. box: □ and ✓, done items dimmed and struck through. progress: ticks with a done-count bar above each list.

rtl.title: Right-to-left terminal
rtl.description: Hebrew and Arabic get a right-to-left layout (right aligned, bullets and quote bars on the right, tables mirrored), with the letters sent the way your terminal needs them. auto detects the terminal; pick one to force its handling, or off for none.

highlightNumbers.title: Highlight numbers
highlightNumbers.description: Color versions, IDs, counts and durations in prose and tables.

accentColor.title: Accent
accentColor.description: Color for the reply bullet, H3+ headings and quote bars. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

headingColor.title: Heading
headingColor.description: Color for H1 and H2 headings. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

tableHeaderColor.title: Table header
tableHeaderColor.description: Color for table header cells. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

tableRuleColor.title: Table rule
tableRuleColor.description: Color for table rules. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

numberColor.title: Numbers
numberColor.description: Color for versions, IDs and counts. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

pathColor.title: Paths
pathColor.description: Color for file paths. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

linkColor.title: Links
linkColor.description: Color for links and URLs. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

inlineCodeColor.title: Inline code
inlineCodeColor.description: Color for `inline code`. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

codeCommandColor.title: Code command
codeCommandColor.description: Color for the command word in shell blocks. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

codeFlagColor.title: Code flag
codeFlagColor.description: Color for --flags in shell blocks. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

codeStringColor.title: Code string
codeStringColor.description: Color for quoted strings in shell blocks. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

strongColor.title: Bold text
strongColor.description: Color for **bold** text. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

quoteColor.title: Quote
quoteColor.description: Color for block quotes. Hex (#a6e3a1), rgb(166,227,161), ansi256(114) or a name (green). Empty uses the theme.

mermaidAscii.title: Mermaid ASCII only
mermaidAscii.description: Draw diagrams with + - | > instead of box-drawing characters, for fonts without them.

diagramColor.title: Diagram lines
diagramColor.description: Color for diagram boxes and arrows. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme.

diagramTextColor.title: Diagram text
diagramTextColor.description: Color for diagram labels and LaTeX formulas. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme.

toolRows.title: Tool rows
toolRows.description: Draw tool calls as one compact line: Ran gh pr view 12, Read ~/src/app.ts, Edited README.md. Results still draw below as usual.

emphasisColor.title: Italic text
emphasisColor.description: Color for *italic* text. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme.

codeTextColor.title: Code text
codeTextColor.description: Color for code block text. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme.

codeCommentColor.title: Code comment
codeCommentColor.description: Color for # comments in shell blocks. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme.

ruleColor.title: Rules
ruleColor.description: Color for horizontal rules, diff card borders and chart gridlines. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme.

bulletColor.title: Bullets
bulletColor.description: Color for list bullets and numbers. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme.

diffAddedColor.title: Diff added
diffAddedColor.description: Color for added diff lines: their + marks and count, and in hex the tint behind them, mixed into black or white so code text stays at 4.5:1. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme's green.

diffRemovedColor.title: Diff removed
diffRemovedColor.description: Color for removed diff lines: their - marks and count, and in hex the tint behind them, mixed into black or white so code text stays at 4.5:1. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the theme's red.

replyBulletColor.title: Reply bullet
replyBulletColor.description: Color for the ● before each reply. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the accent color.

heading1Color.title: H1
heading1Color.description: Color for H1 headings only. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the heading color.

heading2Color.title: H2
heading2Color.description: Color for H2 headings only. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the heading color.

heading3Color.title: H3
heading3Color.description: Color for H3 headings only. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the accent color.

heading4Color.title: H4
heading4Color.description: Color for H4 headings only. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the accent color (the bold text color in the banner style).

heading5Color.title: H5
heading5Color.description: Color for H5 headings only. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the accent color (the bold text color in the banner style).

heading6Color.title: H6
heading6Color.description: Color for H6 headings only. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses the accent color (the bold text color in the banner style).

turnDurationColor.title: Turn footer
turnDurationColor.description: One color for the whole ✻ Worked for 8s · 14:32 line after each turn. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty keeps the words in the comment color and the duration and time in the number color.

diffStyle.title: Diff style
diffStyle.description: How edit and shell edit diffs draw. card: a rounded box with tinted lines. full: no box, each changed line tinted across the width. marks: no box and no tint, only the +/- marks in the theme's diff colors. bar: no box and no tint, a colored ▌ before each changed line. Every style highlights the code and marks the changed words.

diffWidth.title: Diff width
diffWidth.description: fit: a diff card is as wide as its longest line. full (fork): every card spans the window, its tinted lines too, so cards line up.

diffFold.title: Diff folding
diffFold.description: none: a diff card always shows its lines. open (fork): a click anywhere on the card folds it to its head line, and another opens it; it starts open. folded (fork): it starts as the head line, a click opens it. Applies to created files too with createdStyle card.

diffTint.title: Diff tint
diffTint.description: How strongly added and removed lines are tinted (fork): the percent of the diff color in their background, 0 to 60, lowered further where code text would drop below 4.5:1; 0 leaves the lines on the card's ground and tints only the changed words. Empty keeps 30 on dark themes and 20 on light ones.

diffWordTint.title: Diff word tint
diffWordTint.description: How strongly the changed words stand out from their line (fork): the percent of the diff color laid over the line's tint, 0 to 90. Empty keeps 30.

proseCap.title: Cap prose width
proseCap.description: Wrap paragraphs, lists, quotes and alerts at proseWidth columns, a comfortable reading measure, however wide the window (fork). Headings, code, tables, diagrams, figures and cards keep the whole width.

proseWidth.title: Prose width
proseWidth.description: The column at which capped prose wraps, a whole number from 40 to 200 (fork). Required while proseCap is on: a missing or invalid value stops prismantis loading, with this option named. 65 to 80 is the classic comfortable measure.

toolWidth.title: Tool row width
toolWidth.description: With toolStyle chat, tool rows line up on the right edge at this many columns, or at the window's edge when the window is narrower (fork), a whole number from 40 to 400. Empty keeps the window's edge; an invalid value stops prismantis loading, with this option named.

diffToggle.title: Diff toggle
diffToggle.description: card: a click on a diff card folds or opens it. row (fork): a click on the Edit or Write row ('Edited path ●') does it instead; a folded card is then not drawn at all and an open one shows only its lines, the row being its head. Needs diffFold open or folded; cards of shell edits keep their own toggle.

answerMark.title: Mark the answer
answerMark.description: Once a turn ends, draw a heavy rule across the window above its final answer and dim its step lines, the short lines Claude writes before tool calls, and the summary rows Claude Code draws in place of such text (fork). Read from the transcript at each turn's end and at session start, the last 500 turns only; a turn with no step line is left as is, a turn that ends on a tool call (interrupted) has no answer, and a line Claude wrote in more than one turn is never marked.

stepMark.title: Mark each step
stepMark.description: Once a turn ends, draw a dim thin rule across the window above each of its step lines but the first, so every step (a short line and the tool rows after it) reads as its own block (fork). A summary row Claude Code draws in place of a step line always gets one, as its place in the turn is unknown. Read from the transcript like answerMark; works with or without it.

editErrors.title: Failed edit errors
editErrors.description: shown: a failed Edit or Write prints its error under its row. folded (fork, with diffToggle row, a diffFold other than none and toolOutput not quiet): the error sits behind the row like a diff card, opened by a click on the row, whose ' failed' already tells; diffFold sets whether it starts open.

editRow.title: Edit row
editRow.description: path: an Edit or Write row shows the file's path as it is. file (fork): the folder dim, the file name highlighted, then the change's +N −M (a created file counts its lines).

createdStyle.title: Created file style
createdStyle.description: preview: a created file shows its first lines under 'Created path (N lines)', the rest behind a button. card (fork): it draws as an edit's diff card does, same width, border and fold (diffFold, a click anywhere toggles it), on createdBackgroundColor, else diffBackgroundColor.

createdBackgroundColor.title: Created file card background
createdBackgroundColor.description: Background of a created file's card (createdStyle card, fork). Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty uses diffBackgroundColor.

diffBorder.title: Diff card border
diffBorder.description: Draw the rounded border of a diff card (diffStyle card). Off, with diffBackgroundColor set, the card is a filled block; off without it, the lines stand alone (fork).

diffPath.title: Diff file name
diffPath.description: Put the edited file's path before the +N −M counts on an edit's diff card (fork); shell edit cards always show it.

diffBackgroundColor.title: Diff card background
diffBackgroundColor.description: Background of a diff card (diffStyle card, fork); the added and removed tints are mixed into it. Hex, rgb(), ansi256() or a name. Empty leaves the terminal's background.

pieStyle.title: Pie style
pieStyle.description: How mermaid pie charts draw. round: a circle with a legend, falling back to bars in ascii mode, with more slices than the theme has distinct colors (mono always) or in a narrow terminal. bars: one bar per slice, largest first, with its share.

mermaid.title: Mermaid diagrams
mermaid.description: Draw ```mermaid blocks as colored box art sized to the terminal. Off leaves the code as written.

copyButtons.title: Copy buttons
copyButtons.description: Put a copy button on code blocks, tables, diagrams, lists and quotes. Reach them with ctrl+x tab then Enter, or click where the terminal passes clicks through.

copyButtonStyle.title: Copy button style
copyButtonStyle.description: inline: buttons beside or above each block, always shown. hover: each block shows a dim ⧉ beside its first row, and the reply one in its bottom-right corner; the pointer on a ⧉ draws its buttons over it, so they take no line; ctrl+x tab does not reach them, and the mobile app, which has no pointer, shows them inline. icon (fork): as hover, but a marker with a single action is that action, so a click on it copies at once. Needs copyButtons on.

issueHint.title: Issue hint
issueHint.description: On your first prompt and every tenth after it, tell the model it can offer, after asking you, to open a minimal repro issue on prismantis when you say something drew wrong. About 35 tokens each time.

handoff.title: Hand-off blocks
handoff.description: Draw ```handoff blocks (CLAUDE: and CMD: entries Claude hands you to run) as one card at the end of the reply, Claude Code inputs first, each with a copy icon; a one-line slash command also gets a ▷ that runs it in the session. A block with any problem is not drawn as a card: it stays code, under a red line per problem and one naming where the format is. Off leaves them as code.

drafts.title: Draft cards
drafts.description: Draw ```draft blocks (a prompt for another session, an email, a chat message or a GitHub comment you send yourself) as a card titled by its kind, the body drawn as markdown, with a copy button that copies the body exactly as written (and one for an email's subject), and a red line for every malformed header. Off leaves them as code.

copyIcon.title: Copy icon
copyIcon.description: The glyph of a copy marker: on hand-off and draft cards, beside the turn footer, and on hover markers. A marker with one action copies on click; one with several opens them. One terminal cell wide, e.g. a Nerd Font icon such as . Empty uses ⧉.

replyIcon.title: Reply icon
replyIcon.description: The glyph before the first line of a reply text, what Claude writes to you (fork). One terminal cell wide, e.g. a Nerd Font icon. Empty uses ●.

thinkingIcon.title: Thinking icon
thinkingIcon.description: The glyph before a summary row, the line Claude Code draws between tool calls in place of Claude's thinking or text (with thinkingDisplay updates, the thinking) (fork). One terminal cell wide. Empty uses ●.

toolIcon.title: Tool icon
toolIcon.description: The status glyph of a finished tool row, colored by how the call ended (fork); a running call keeps ◌. One terminal cell wide, e.g. a Nerd Font icon. Empty uses ●.

runIcon.title: Run icon
runIcon.description: The glyph of the run mark a hand-off card puts on a slash command entry, before its copy icon. One terminal cell wide, e.g. a Nerd Font icon. Empty uses ▷.

turnWord.title: Turn footer word
turnWord.description: A fixed word for the line that closes a turn, drawn without the ✻: Ran gives 'Ran for 5m 54s'. Empty keeps Claude Code's changing word (✻ Baked for …).

replyCopy.title: Copy reply
replyCopy.description: Where the button that copies a whole reply sits. message: under each multi-block message. footer: on the terminal, a copy icon right after the turn footer (✻ Baked for … · 18:31), copying the turn's final answer; other surfaces keep message. Needs copyButtons on.

diagramHints.title: Diagram hints
diagramHints.description: Attach a short note, read by the model and never shown, to each prompt you type or another plugin sends, saying tables, code, mermaid diagrams, charts and figures render here, and LaTeX formulas when the renderer runs. About 630 tokens per prompt (about 275 for the main part, about 360 for figures), about 80 more with LaTeX. Off when mermaid is off.

latex.title: LaTeX math
latex.description: Draw $$ and ```math formulas as typeset images in kitty and Ghostty (not under tmux) with RaTeX's renderer, installed as ratex-render on your PATH. Off runs nothing. Formulas that can't be drawn stay as text.
